newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARTINEZ LEADS YANKS PAST TRIBE 11-10.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARTINEZ LEADS YANKS PAST TRIBE 11-10.

text.p: Tino Martinez hit a three-run homer in the first and drove in the winning run in the eighth to lead the New York Yankees to a 11-10 victory over Cleveland Indians on Sunday.
The teams combined for 21 runs and 28 hits after combining for 20 runs in Cleveland's 12-8 win on Saturday as pitchers were fair game throughout the series.

After Cleveland tied the game 10-10 in the top of the eighth, Paul O'Neill beat out an infield single and moved to third on Cecil Fielder's single to start the Yanks' final rally. Paul Assenmacher relieved Jose Mesa (0-4) and Martinez singled to right, scoring pinch-runner Pat Kelly.
"We never gave up. No matter how far we got down, we knew we could come back," said Martinez, whose team trailed 7-3 early in the game.

Martinez had given the Yankees a 3-1 lead when he launched Jason Jacome's 2-2 pitch into the right-field upper deck for 28th homer, leaving him just one behind major league-leader Ken Griffey of Seattle.
The Yankees also got a three-run homer from Charlie Hayes in the third.

Cleveland erupted for five runs in the second on a two-run double by Kevin Seitzer and a three-run double by Manny Ramirez off Yankee starter David Cone, who had been virtually untouchable in his previous three starts.
"There's just no easy way explain it really," said Cone, who gave up seven runs. "It can be a humbling game sometimes."
Mariano Rivera (2-2) blew the save but picked up the win.
In Boston, Darren Bragg doubled home the tie-breaking run and scored on a single by Mike Stanley in the seventh inning as the Red Sox beat the Detroit Tigers 8-6.
Troy O'Leary doubled twice and drove in three runs and Stanley added two RBI for the Red Sox.
John Wasdin (3-3) picked up the win despite allowing a run and three hits in 1 2/3 innings. Detroit reliever Jose Bautista (1-2) took the loss.

In Baltimore, sacrifice flies by Otis Nixon, Charlie O'Brien and Joe Carter gave reliever Kelvim Escobar his first major league win as the Toronto Blue Jays completed a four-game sweep of the Orioles with a 3-2 victory.
Carter's sacrifice fly off Armando Benitez (0-3) in the eighth plated Carlos Garcia with the winning run.
Escobar made his major league debut in the fourth inning and allowed one run and two hits in 4 1/3 innings.

In Kansas City, pinch-hitter Antone Williamson singled home the tying run and scored the go-ahead run on Jeff Huson's two-out single in the top of the ninth inning as the Milwaukee Brewers rallied for a 3-2 victory over the Royals.
Royals reliever Jeff Montgomery (0-3) began the ninth with a 2-1 lead but allowed a single by pinch-hitter Matt Mieske, who scored on Williamson's single.
With Williamson on third and two-out, Huson slapped the first pitch to centre field for the winning run.
Bob Wickman (5-3) pitched a scoreless eighth for the win.

At Minnesota, centre fielder Mike Cameron robbed Roberto Kelly of the tying home run in the bottom of the eighth and Chris Snopek and Dave Martinez each had two hits and two RBI as the surging Chicago White Sox beat the Twins 6-4.
Chicago had a two-run lead in the eighth when Kelly, with a man on base, lined a 1-2 pitch to deep centre. Cameron leaped and snared it backhanded while it was over the fence.
Roberto Hernandez breezed through the ninth for his 19th save, preserving the win for Wilson Alvarez (7-6).
With its eighth win in nine games, Chicago moved within one game of first-place Cleveland in the Central Division.
In Seattle, rookie Jose Cruz Jr hit a solo homer with two out in the bottom of the ninth inning to lift the Mariners to a 3-2 win over the Anaheim Angels.
Paul Sorrento also hit a solo homer for Seattle.
With the score knotted 2-2, Cruz drilled a 1-2 pitch from Rich DeLucia (6-3) over the wall in right field as the Mariners posted their club-record 20th victory of the month.
Bobby Ayala (5-2) pitched out of a bases-loaded, none-out in the top of the ninth and earned the win.
In Oakland, pinch-hitter Mark Bellhorn's bloop single to shallow left field scored Scott Spiezio in a five-run eighth inning to rally the Athletics past the Texas Rangers 7-5.
A solo homer by Matt Stairs started the raly, pulling Oakland within 5-3. RBI singles by Jason Giambi and Dave Magadan tied the game before Belhorn's single put the Athletics ahead to stay.
Oakland's Mark McGwire belted his 29th homer in the second, tying him with Griffey for the major-league lead.
Carlos Reyes (3-0) allowed a run and three hits over three innings in relief of starter Steve Karsay for the win.
